lesson.menu_title: What Are You Into? — Your Life Right Now
lesson.menu_desc: Two courses, one semester, and the tense for what you are in the middle of -- 36 slides
lesson.subtitle: Lesson 4 -- What Are You Into?
lesson.title_tag: Professor View -- Giovanna Waltrick | Lesson 4 -- What Are You Into?

listenings.text: I work for a small brand and we launch two collections a year, which sounds calm until you understand what it means. Right now, in August, I am working on next winter. The pieces in our shop windows today were finished eleven months ago, and honestly I barely remember them. That is the hardest part of this job, and nobody warns you about it at school: you live in two times at once. You talk to customers about a collection you finished last year while your head is inside one that nobody has seen. If I could give students one piece of advice, it would not be about drawing or about trends. It would be this: learn to read a calendar as well as you read a trend. The people who last in this industry are not the ones with the best ideas. They are the ones whose ideas arrive on the right date.

I am doing two courses at the same time, and the question I get most is why. The honest answer is that I did not want to spend four years finding out whether I had chosen the right thing. So I am doing both, and I am letting them tell me. People imagine the hard part is the hours. It is not. The hours are fine, because the two courses happen at different times of day. The hard part is the weeks when both of them have deadlines together, and there is no version of that week where I do everything well. Everybody keeps telling me to choose one. What I have noticed is that the two courses explain each other. The business one tells me why a good idea dies, and the creative one tells me why a well-managed company can still be boring. So no, I am not choosing yet.
